model: Series GSTC carbon monoxide / nitrogen dioxide gas transmitter, BACnet MS/TP
applies_to: Dwyer Series GSTC carbon monoxide (GSTC-C) and nitrogen dioxide (GSTC-N) gas transmitters with switch-selectable BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU.
summary: The GSTC is an electrochemical CO or NO2 transmitter for parking garages and similar spaces. A DIP switch picks BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU. Over BACnet it has one Analog Input for the gas level in ppm, a Binary Value to zero the sensor and two Date Values the user fills in for the calibration and sensor replacement dates.
notes: AI 1 is named "CO Concentration" on CO models and "NO2 Concentration" on NO2 models.
Calibration Date and Replace Sensor Date are BACnet Date Value objects (DV 1, DV 2), listed here as Other.
The Date Values are not tracked by the transmitter; someone has to write them after field calibration or sensor replacement.
The BV 1 property table shows Present_Value as Read, but the text says writing it active zeroes the sensor; marked writable here.

source.title: Series GSTC Carbon Monoxide / Nitrogen Dioxide Gas Transmitter - Specifications, Installation and Operating Instructions

integration.summary: Set the address and BACnet protocol on the DIP switches and read AI 1 for the gas level in ppm. Alarm and fan logic live in the BMS.

minimum_points.name: CO Concentration
minimum_points.why: Gas level, ppm (CO or NO2 by model)

setup: Address and protocol (BACnet or Modbus) are set on the DIP switches; valid BACnet addresses are 1-127.
Device instance defaults to 607xxx, where xxx is the DIP switch address.
Auto-baud detects the bus speed after power-up.
DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice need the password "Dwyer".
gotchas: Electrochemical sensors drift; Dwyer recommends recalibration every 6 months (5% accuracy holds at 12-month intervals).
